stories-43-46-56-pharaoh-boasting-do-not.title: Pharaoh Boasting to Moses: Do Not These Rivers of Egypt Flow Beneath Me
stories-43-46-56-pharaoh-boasting-do-not.note: Surah 43:46–56 places into the mouth of the Exodus Pharaoh confronting Moses the boast 'Is the kingdom of Egypt not mine, and these rivers which flow beneath me,' attributing to him Pharaoh Hophra's Nile boast in Ezekiel 29:2–3.

discussion.view: Muslim commentators explain that Rameses or the Pharaoh of the Exodus boasted before his assembly of Egypt's Nile canals and tributaries to belittle Moses prior to the drowning in the Red Sea.
discussion.reply: In the Hebrew Bible, the Pharaoh of the Exodus confronts Moses by the Nile (Exodus 5:2; 7:15), whereas the specific boast 'The rivers are mine, and I made them' belongs to Pharaoh Hophra (Apries, r. 589–570 BC) in Ezekiel 29:2–3 and 29:9, more than six centuries after the Exodus.

stories-43-46-56-pharaoh-boasting-do-not.quranEn: [46] Certainly We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his assembly. He said, ‘Surely I am a messenger of the Lord of the worlds.’ [47] But when he brought them Our signs, suddenly they began to laugh at them, [48] even though every sign We showed them was greater than the one before it. We seized them with the punishment, so that they might return. [49] They said, ‘Magician! Call on your Lord for us by whatever covenant He has made with you, (and) surely we shall indeed be (rightly) guided.’ [50] But when We removed the punishment from them, immediately they broke (their promise). [51] Pharaoh called out among his people: ‘My people! Is the kingdom of Egypt not mine, and these rivers (which) flow beneath me? Do you not see? [52] Am I not better than this (man), who is despicable and scarcely makes (things) clear? [53] If only bracelets of gold were cast (down) on him or the accompanying angels came with him.’ [54] So he unsettled his people, and they obeyed him. Surely they were a wicked people. [55] When they had angered Us, We took vengeance on them and drowned them – all (of them)! [56] We made them a thing of the past, and an example for the later (generations).

sources.title: Septuagint (LXX2012) - Ezekiel
sources.en: Son of man, set your face against Pharao king of Egypt, and prophesy against him, and against the whole of Egypt: and say, Thus says the Lord; Behold, I am against Pharao, the great dragon that lies in the midst of his rivers, that says, The rivers are mine, and I made them.
highlights: Behold, I am against Pharao, the great dragon that lies in the midst of his rivers, that says, The rivers are mine, and I made them.
